work.permit: a licence granted by the Minister

note: Read 2026-11-03 on jerseylaw.je (the Jersey Legal Information Board; plain requests met its firewall and the consolidations were read through a fetching service). Work: the Children (Regulation of Employment) (Jersey) Order 2011: a child, for the Order, is under sixteen and below the upper limit of compulsory school age (Art. 1); none under thirteen may be employed in any capacity (Art. 2), and from thirteen a child may work only within the Order's limits (not held). The form's 16 is the age at which a person is no longer a 'child' under the Order, as Great Britain's is held. Performers: the Children (Jersey) Law 2002, Art. 50: a child under sixteen may take part in a performance only under a licence granted by the Minister (no lowest age set). Majority: null here; the person research's (research/sources/person/ages/JE.json) is read; the Age of Majority (Jersey) Law 1999, Art. 1, read the same day, gives eighteen too. Service: not read (the game doesn't read service).

sources.title: Children (Regulation of Employment) (Jersey) Order 2011, Arts. 1 and 2, consolidated from 6 April 2026 (Jersey Legal Information Board)
sources.said: “child” means a person who has not attained the age of 16 years ... is below the upper limit of compulsory school age, as defined in Article 2 of the Education (Jersey) Law 1999 ... A child who is under the age of 13 years shall not be employed in any capacity.

sources.title: Children (Jersey) Law 2002, Part 6, Art. 50, consolidated (Jersey Legal Information Board)
sources.said: a child under the age of 16 years shall not take part in a performance ... except under the authority of a licence granted by the Minister
